summary:
The Assam Roofed Turtle once glided through the clear, cool streams of the Brahmaputra valley's forested foothills, a small and secretive reptile adapted to one of the narrowest ranges of any turtle in South Asia. Found only in scattered pockets of Bangladesh, India, and Bhutan below 200 meters elevation, it asked for little — just clean water, intact forest, and time.

That time has been cut cruelly short. Hunted for food and captured for the luxury pet trade, its populations have collapsed by an estimated 80% across just three generations. Siltation and habitat loss have silenced the streams it called home. Today, only fragments remain, isolated within protected areas, still quietly disappearing.
